All 154 tests pass, lint is clean.

## Summary

Investigated the frontend's existing refresh-token implementation (`src/services/http.js`, `src/store/authStore.js`, `src/shared/hooks/useAuth.js`) against the backend contract (`/tmp/sage-refs/life-cycle-backend`): the reactive 401-retry-via-refresh-cookie flow was already correctly wired (verified with a behavioral test exercising the full fetch-401-refresh-retry sequence), and CORS/cookie settings line up on the backend side. The gap was that renewal only happened *reactively*, after a request already failed with 401 — there was no proactive renewal "when it expires" as the request asked for.

Added proactive token renewal to `src/services/http.js`:
- `readTokenExpiry` decodes the JWT's `exp` claim client-side (no new dependency).
- `scheduleProactiveRefresh` sets a timer to call `refreshSession()` ~60s before the token's actual expiry, rescheduling itself after every successful refresh.
- `clearScheduledRefresh` cancels the timer on logout or when a refresh ultimately fails (session cleared).

Wired it into `src/shared/hooks/useAuth.js` so a fresh login also schedules its own proactive renewal, and logout cancels the pending timer. The existing reactive 401-retry path is left untouched as a fallback for cases where the token lacks a readable `exp` or the proactive refresh was missed.

Added `src/services/http.test.js` covering: 401-retry success, refresh failure clearing the session, the proactive timer firing before expiry, and rescheduling after a successful refresh. Full test suite (154 tests), lint, and production build all pass.
